claims.text: Single-phase ZrB2 requires preparation temperatures above 2300 °C for densification.
Single-phase ZrB2 is prone to pores during extended liquid plating-bath exposure.
Single-phase ZrB2 has limited mechanical strength under extended liquid-bath exposure.
Adding approximately 15–20 vol% fine-grained SiC to ZrB2 lowers its required densification temperature below 2300 °C.
The ZrB2–SiC composite can densify at approximately 1900–2000 °C under 30–50 MPa uniaxial pressure in an inert atmosphere.
Hot pressing or spark plasma sintering is suitable for co-sintering ZrB2 with 15–20 vol% fine SiC.
The selected processing route produces fine SiC particulates dispersed in the ZrB2 matrix.
SiC promotes earlier densification of ZrB2.
Dispersed SiC hinders crack propagation in the ZrB2 matrix.
Dispersed SiC inhibits porosity formation in the ZrB2 matrix.
Reduced porosity and fewer infiltration channels reduce plating-bath fluid infiltration.
Reduced cracking and porosity improve the mechanical strength and integrity of the composite.
Compared with conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2, the composite will exhibit fewer pores.
Compared with conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2, the composite will have greater resistance to liquid infiltration and component failure.
Single-phase ZrB2 prepared above 2300 °C has weaker strength and greater susceptibility to subsurface holes after plating-bath exposure than the proposed composite.
